text: Your conveyor motor runs eight hours a day.
What if a better motor did the same job, with less electricity?
Here's what we know. Output: seven point five kilowatts. Eight hours a day.
Old motor: seventy five percent efficient. New motor: ninety percent.
The trick: the output stays the same.
So input equals output, divided by efficiency.
Old motor: seven point five, divided by zero point seven five: ten kilowatts in.
New motor: seven point five, divided by zero point nine: eight point three three kilowatts in.
Now, times eight hours.
Old: eighty kilowatt hours a day. New: sixty six point seven.
You save thirteen point three kilowatt hours, every single day.
Over two hundred and fifty days, that's about three thousand, three hundred and thirty three kilowatt hours.
About one thousand, six hundred and sixty seven ringgit a year, from one motor.
So, four smart moves for motors.
Upgrade, to I E three or I E four.
Right size: match the real load.
Maintain: bearings, lubrication, alignment.
And switch off when not needed.
But remember:
a new motor cannot fix a bad system, like an oversized pump.
Your turn. Five kilowatts output, ten hours a day. Efficiency goes from seventy, to eighty eight percent.
Energy saved per day? Pause now.
Old: seventy one point four. New: fifty six point eight. You save fourteen point six kilowatt hours a day.
Remember: every kilowatt hour counts.
